en: We take pride in our service, you know.
Come by the shop if you can, eh?
Hmph, how base humans are.
This man thinks of nothing but money.
Become my servant and toil for me.
note: No used_in: decoder seems to miss this box; read as the stern player speaking about Craig between msg 103531 and 103547 (#2962-#2967 one monologue).

en: That would serve the world and its people.
Not that the good of the human world
is anything worth my thinking about.
No, this is our first meeting.
Is this where you do business?
I see... Another time, then.
I have no money with me just now.
Yes, I'm
Do you remember me?
He has no idea what a clock is worth.
That customers pay for a clock's worth
note: #2975/#2976 continue 'He has no idea...' from the box before.

en: more than for the clock itself, see.
I think I'll have a look at your clocks.
It's not fair of me to always just browse.
They'll palm a busted clock off on you.
, my master. Your orders?
note: After the name (Warren as servant): 'Chris, my master. Your orders?'

en: I'll see to anything you ask.
At times I feel surprisingly light,
then so sluggish I can't move at all.
It's as if this body weren't my own.
Give me your orders...
Ah, it must be my age
My body just won't do as it's told.
Well, now, I don't believe I know you.
I have only just come to London.
So it would seem.
I've lived in this city 63 years now.
My name's Warren.
I run the optician's shop.
We're closed just now.
note: Made a full sentence so #2995 (used alone in 107281/107302/107734) and #3044 can start with a capital.

en: Come back when the shop's open.
Ah, you've come.
But the shop isn't open just now.
Care to watch me polish lenses?
The lenses I polish
are the most precise in these parts.
Interested after all, eh?
Then why won't you buy anything
Welcome. In need of spectacles?
No, forgive me, but
I have no need of spectacles.
I see. Well, it can't be helped.
But I've not seen your face round here.
I'm Warren.
I run this optician's, as you can see.
Ah, you've come. What spectacles suit you?
No, I merely dropped by again today.
Well, then, I'll look out for
something you might buy.
Welcome. Spectacles...
note: Followed by #396 'Ah, ' + name + #101 ', it's you.' on the next line.

en: You've no need of spectacles, as I recall.
But an optician sells more
than just spectacles,
as I'll show you one of these days.
This microscope here. Might you want it?
A powerful microscope I polished with care.
You'll find none finer in all London.
No, I have no need of it.
I never have cause to examine
anything so small.
No need, eh? What a pity.
, I've been waiting for you.
These tinted spectacles, said to come from Asia.
note: #3028 follows on the same line, so this row ends with a space.

en: What do you think?
They say they were used to hide one's eye
movements from others. Quite rare, but
No, those are not for me either.
I have no need to hide these eyes.
I see. So you don't want them after all.
With these, you could even shut out
dazzling light, you know.
Business truly is a contest, eh?
I won't give up until you buy something.
I've only just come to London.
So it seems. My name's Warren.
